gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the big stations' own measured inverter idle draw (52 W DELTA Pro Ultra, 58-85 W Jackery 5000 Plus, about 20 W BLUETTI Apex 300) is as large as or larger than a 40-50 W fan, so counted per night it roughly halves ChatGPT's 10-16-night figures for the EcoFlow, Jackery and Anker picks and makes the $5,399 BLUETTI Apex 300 + 2x B500K (13,004.8 Wh, about 23 nights of a 50 W fan) the most nights per unit and per dollar.
standout_why: Compared against the cited Solar Waypoint F3800 vs DELTA Pro Ultra vs 5000 Plus comparison (capacity only, no prices, no idle draw, no runtimes) and RuntimeWise's home-backup list (capacity, list price and Wh per list dollar for 17 models, runtimes 'calculated, not measured', no idle draw). ChatGPT's own answers divide rated Wh x 85% by the fan alone and only mention idle draw as a hedge; GearSpec Outpost's expandable-capacity article returned HTTP 429, so it was not checked.
decides: It changes the pick. Counting each station's own idle draw for 8 h a night with a 50 W fan: BLUETTI Apex 300 + 2x B500K about 23 nights for $5,399 (about $233 per night of runtime); Apex 300 + B500K about 14 nights for $3,599; DELTA Pro Ultra about 7.5 nights for $3,699 instead of ChatGPT's 13; Jackery 5000 Plus about 4.7-5.8 nights instead of 10, at $3,499 and on pre-order; Anker F3800 Plus about 3.7-5.2 nights instead of 8, sold out. The DELTA Pro Ultra X and Anker E10 hold about 12 kWh, but no measured idle draw was found for either, so the Apex 300 + 2x B500K is the largest system whose nights can actually be worked out. It costs $2,500 less than the DPU X and still has more Wh.
